intro: Stories about our research written for a general audience, from science news outlets and university press offices. Newest first.

items.title: Holographic mesoscope reads, writes from different cortical regions simultaneously
items.author: Simon Makin
items.summary: The tool could help reveal how information transmission between areas relates to perception, cognition and behavior.
items.paper: Probing inter-areal computations with a cellular resolution two-photon holographic mesoscope

items.title: Holographic optogenetics could enable faster brain mapping for new discoveries
items.author: Ingrid Fadelli
items.summary: Coverage of a collaboration between the Paninski and Adesnik labs on using holographic stimulation of neural ensembles, together with compressed sensing, to map synaptic connectivity much faster.
items.paper: Rapid learning of neural circuitry from holographic ensemble stimulation enabled by model-based compressed sensing

items.title: Bombarding Brain Cells with Lasers, Scientists Pinpoint the Source of Illusions, Revealing New Insights Into Schizophrenia
items.author: Ryan Whalen
items.summary: How a small set of neurons in visual cortex lets the brain fill in edges that aren’t really there — and what that could mean for understanding hallucinations.
items.paper: Recurrent pattern completion drives the neocortical representation of sensory inference

items.title: Scientists shine a laser light on the brain cells that show us illusions
items.author: Alan Boyle
items.summary: Researchers at UC Berkeley and Seattle’s Allen Institute identify the “illusion neurons” that help the brain see shapes that aren’t actually present.
items.paper: Recurrent pattern completion drives the neocortical representation of sensory inference

items.title: Brain illusion: US scientists use lasers to reveal how we see what isn’t there
items.author: Mrigakshi Dixit
items.summary: Stimulating “IC-encoder” neurons with light recreated the brain activity of viewing an optical illusion, even with no illusion on the screen.
items.paper: Recurrent pattern completion drives the neocortical representation of sensory inference

items.title: Scientists shoot lasers into brain cells to uncover how illusions work
items.author: Peter Kim
items.summary: Supported by the Allen Institute’s OpenScope program, the findings could help us better understand neuropsychiatric disorders like schizophrenia and reshape our understanding of vision.
items.paper: Recurrent pattern completion drives the neocortical representation of sensory inference

items.title: Null and Noteworthy: Downstream brain areas read visual cortex signals en masse in mice
items.author: Laura Dattaro
items.summary: The finding contradicts a theory that the regions prioritize neurons that are adept at identifying specific stimuli.
items.paper: Network influence determines the impact of cortical ensembles on stimulus detection

items.title: Mind-blowing science: ‘Star Wars-style’ holograms to communicate with the brain
items.summary: On the holographic neurotechnology platform being developed by Hillel Adesnik, Laura Waller and Rikky Muller for two-way communication with the brain — what Hillel calls a “Hubble telescope for the brain.”

items.title: Researchers are developing a device that can edit brain activity
items.author: Tristan Greene
items.summary: How projecting holograms into the brain lets researchers switch groups of about 50 neurons on and off, hundreds of times per second.
items.paper: Precise multimodal optical control of neural ensemble activity

items.title: Editing brain activity with holography
items.summary: UC Berkeley neuroscientists use holographic projection to activate or suppress dozens of neurons at once, copying real patterns of brain activity.
items.paper: Precise multimodal optical control of neural ensemble activity

items.title: A mouse’s view of the world, seen through its whiskers
items.summary: Neurons in the mouse somatosensory cortex build a smooth map of the space around the head as the whiskers scan it, not just a map of the whiskers themselves.
items.paper: Surround integration organizes a spatial map during active sensation

items.title: Incredible brain-controlling microscope revealed
items.author: Tim Newman
items.summary: A microscope that can watch the activity of individual brain cells with millisecond precision, and switch those same cells on and off with light.

items.title: Novel IR microscope can manipulate neural activity in live animals
items.summary: An infrared microscope built at UC Berkeley that controls the firing of individual neurons in the living brain, to decode how neural signals give rise to brain function.
